narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: The evangelist: narration, speech introductions, glosses and his own reflections.

mary.name: Mary
mary.note: The mother of Jesus at Cana; quiet, confident request.

jesus.name: Jesus
jesus.note: The Lord; calm authority, patient with those who misunderstand him.

chief-steward.name: Chief steward of the feast
chief-steward.note: Master of the wedding feast at Cana; pleasantly surprised, jovial to the bridegroom.

the-jews.name: The Jews
the-jews.note: The Jewish authorities in the temple; challenging and incredulous.

1.t: And the third day, there was a marriage in Cana of Galilee: and the mother of Jesus was there.

2.t: And Jesus also was invited, and his disciples, to the marriage.

3.t: And the wine failing, the mother of Jesus saith to him:

4.t: Woman, what is that to me and to thee? My hour is not yet come.

5.t: His mother saith to the waiters:
Whatsoever he shall say to you, do ye.

6.t: Now there were set there six waterpots of stone, according to the manner of the purifying of the Jews, containing two or three measures apiece.

7.t: And they filled them up to the brim.

8.t: Draw out now and carry to the chief steward of the feast.

9.t: And when the chief steward had tasted the water made wine and knew not whence it was, but the waiters knew who had drawn the water: the chief steward calleth the bridegroom,

10.t: Every man at first setteth forth good wine, and when men have well drunk, then that which is worse. But thou hast kept the good wine until now.

11.t: This beginning of miracles did Jesus in Cana of Galilee and manifested his glory. And his disciples believed in him.

12.t: After this, he went down to Capharnaum, he and his mother and his brethren and his disciples: and they remained there not many days.

13.t: And the pasch of the Jews was at hand: and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

14.t: And he found in the temple them that sold oxen and sheep and doves, and the changers of money sitting.

15.t: And when he had made, as it were, a scourge of little cords, he drove them all out of the temple, the sheep also and the oxen: and the money of the changers he poured out, and the tables he overthrew.

16.t: And to them that sold doves he said:
Take these things hence, and make not the house of my Father a house of traffic.

17.t: And his disciples remembered, that it was written: The zeal of thy house hath eaten me up.

18.t: The Jews, therefore, answered, and said to him:
What sign dost thou shew unto us, seeing thou dost these things?

19.t: Jesus answered and said to them:
Destroy this temple; and in three days I will raise it up.

20.t: Six and forty years was this temple in building; and wilt thou raise it up in three days?

21.t: But he spoke of the temple of his body.

22.t: When therefore he was risen again from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this: and they believed the scripture and the word that Jesus had said.

23.t: Now when he was at Jerusalem, at the pasch, upon the festival day, many believed in his name, seeing his signs which he did.

24.t: But Jesus did not trust himself unto them: for that he knew all men,

25.t: And because he needed not that any should give testimony of man: for he knew what was in man.
